text:
cam: Quick question — I ran a console-preview for a routing_weight change (model A -> model B, 10% -> 30%) and the snapshot shows a weird estimated-cost delta.
jess: :eyes: what did the delta look like? raw token estimate or the cost after batching heuristics?
cam: The UI shows +8% cost, but our staging traces show almost no latency change and tokens look similar. worried the preview isn't applying batching/caching heuristics.
mike: The preview path should run the same estimator as the router, but there are two modes: cheap_estimate (fast, ignores batching) and runtime_estimate (slower, sim that approximates batching). Which one did you pick?
cam: I used the console default (fast). Maybe that's the problem. But the default label isn't clear to users.
laura: Can we make the toggle explicit? "Estimate mode: fast | runtime (includes batching & KV cache)". Right now it says "Preview accuracy: low/medium" which is vague.
ux-nick: Agreed — UX improvement: show an inline tooltip that says "fast mode does not simulate coalesced batches or prefix cache hits -> may overestimate cost for high concurrency workloads".
jess: More than UX, the API has an inconsistency. The CLI preview endpoint (/v1/configs/preview) accepts ?mode=fast|runtime but the console calls /v1/console/preview which always passes mode=fast for speed. We should consider switching to runtime for routing-weight changes because cost is the main signal.
mike: runtime mode is ~3x slower. For big accounts it times out in the browser. Maybe run runtime mode but async: return quick fast-estimate immediately and then surface a follow-up runtime estimate when ready.
cam: That'd be perfect. Also, when the runtime estimate comes back, we need to highlight "quota headroom" impact. The routing change bumped model B usage in the snapshot and pushes some routes close to their per-model quota.
laura: On quotas — we currently only show per-customer aggregate quota. We should surface per-route and per-model headroom in the preview. That way owners see "this rollout will consume 72% of model-B quota".
jess: Implementation question: do we run preview sampling across the same hashing/cohort algorithm used in rollout? If not, the numbers won't match production.
mike: We currently sample 100k requests from production traces for preview, but we do not apply cohort hashing. Easy fix: replay traces through the same hashing function to compute exact cohort assignments.
cam: Good. One more internal API thought: the promote endpoint for dry-run uses POST /v1/configs/promote?dry_run=true and returns a single summary object. Could we add a field `telemetry_sample_rates` that recommends which metrics to bump during rollout? (e.g., increase sampling of tail latency traces from 1% -> 10%)
laura: That's smart. And tie it to an ops-playbook link. e.g., when promote response includes "risk: model_quota", console shows: "Suggested checks: increase model-quota alert sensitivity; enable detailed traces for 10 minutes post-promote".
ux-nick: UX note: do not overload the main preview pane. Put the recommendations in a collapsible "Ops guidance" card with copy buttons.
ops-bot: deploy-bot: scheduled dry-run preview for config 2026-11-18T14:03Z finished. Summary: fast_estimate + async runtime_estimate requested. runtime_estimate ETA ~45s.
jess: Great — once runtime_estimate lands can someone verify parity with our staging router replay? I can run the replay job.
mike: I'll hook the preview pipeline to emit a trace id so replay can pick the same window: preview_trace_id -> used by replay.
cam: Thanks all. Action items: laura/ux-nick add tooltip + ops card mockups; mike implement async runtime_estimate + trace_id; jess run replay when runtime_estimate done; laura add per-model & per-route quota headroom in preview response.
laura: I'll drop mocks by EOD. :thumbsup:
cam: Appreciate it, folks.
